hero.headline: Israeli forces push into central Gaza to destroy tunnel, prompting Hamas ceasefire breach accusation
hero.body:
Israeli ground forces advanced into central Gaza beyond their occupied zone on Wednesday to dismantle what the military described as a terror tunnel posing an immediate threat to troops. The operation, which took place west of the Yellow Line marking the boundary of the more than 60 percent of Gaza under Israeli control, prompted evacuation orders for residents near Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps. Hamas accused Israel of a flagrant violation of the October 2025 ceasefire agreement.

Witnesses reported tanks advancing east of Nuseirat refugee camp and moving onto the main north-south Salah al-Din road under artillery cover. The Israeli military said the targeted operation aimed to remove an immediate threat and prevent Hamas from harming Israeli civilians or troops. The military body Cogat warned Palestinians in the area to stay away for their own safety and announced the closure of a section of Salah al-Din road.

Footage verified by BBC Verify showed families fleeing near Nuseirat camp, with residents reporting indiscriminate gunfire and shelling. One displaced resident said Israeli forces fired randomly at areas sheltering displaced people, forcing families to leave behind all belongings. Gaza's Hamas-run Civil Defence agency reported three people killed in separate Israeli drone strikes on Wednesday, including one man in Nuseirat. The Israeli military told BBC it had struck several military operatives.

At least 1,658 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since the ceasefire began last year, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry. More than 1.9 million people, about 90 percent of Gaza's population, remain displaced, with 1.4 million living in tents or makeshift shelters. Reconstruction has not begun in Gaza, where an estimated 82 percent of structures have been destroyed or damaged during the war. The disarmament of Hamas remains a key obstacle to advancing a U.S. peace plan.

cards.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigns amid scandal, raising concerns about AI investment and US economic impact
cards.teaser: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs, one allegedly involving a Chinese spy, triggering questions about the chip manufacturer's rol
cards.body:
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs, one allegedly involving a Chinese spy, triggering questions about the chip manufacturer's rol

The scandal wiped hundreds of billions of dollars off Nvidia's stock market value and created uncertainty around the company's future direction. Nvidia, valued at $3.8 trillion, reported Tuesday that quarterly sales doubled from a year earlier.

cards.headline: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 a share, valuing AI company at $1.5 trillion
cards.body:
Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, above its projected range of $70 to $78, valuing the artificial intelligence company at $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis. The company will begin trading Thursday on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.

The pricing reflects strong investor appetite for the AI company despite recent market volatility following the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The $1.5 trillion valuation marks a significant increase from the $965 billion Anthropic reached in May when it raised $65 billion in its last private funding round, though it falls short of the $2 trillion the company reportedly sought several months ago.

Amazon and Google hold the largest stakes in Anthropic, owning nearly 15 percent and almost 14 percent of the company respectively. A group of major technology companies including AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC Partners agreed to purchase $26 billion worth of non-voting shares through a private placement alongside the IPO. Among venture capital investors, Sequoia and former Google CEO Eric Schmidt each reportedly own approximately 1 percent of the company, as does Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC.

The IPO delivers a substantial windfall to Anthropic's numerous backers, though none of its venture capital investors holds more than a 5 percent stake. Each of the company's seven co-founders, including CEO Dario Amodei, sold nearly 3.4 million shares in the offering, bringing in about $282 million per founder according to the S-1 filing. The company's performance is expected to influence expectations for other private AI companies, including rival OpenAI, which was last valued at $1.25 billion and has not announced IPO plans.

cards.headline: Russia warns France and other NATO allies after Paris confirms military personnel in Ukraine
cards.teaser: Moscow says it will treat foreign troops as legitimate targets after France acknowledged sending specialists to maintain weapons systems.
cards.body:
Russia warned it will regard foreign troops in Ukraine as legitimate targets after France confirmed it periodically sends military personnel into Ukraine to maintain weapons systems and provide training. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said the deployments constitute direct participation in the war, not merely support. French officials said the personnel are noncombatants who conduct limited missions to maintain equipment including Mirage aircraft and Caesar howitzers.

France first delivered Mirage fighters to Ukraine last year and has supplied precision bombs, cruise missiles, air defense systems, and other equipment. Lavrov said other nations also have personnel in Ukraine and accused them of providing satellite data and target designation. Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova said Moscow will leave the military to determine a response.

cards.headline: ADNOC oil tanker attacked in Strait of Hormuz, one crew member missing
cards.teaser: An oil tanker operated by ADNOC Logistics & Services was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on the evening of November 17, leaving one crew member unaccounted for and e
cards.body:
An oil tanker operated by ADNOC Logistics & Services was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on the evening of November 17, leaving one crew member unaccounted for and e

All other crew members were safely evacuated from the vessel. The attack marks the second on an ADNOC vessel in recent weeks.

cards.headline: Ukraine's attack on Kerch Strait bridge disrupts Russia's Crimea supply lines
cards.teaser: The collapse of the highway section has blocked shipping traffic and suspended road access, complicating Russian military logistics and drone operations from occupied Crimea.
cards.body:
Ukraine's attack on the Kerch Strait bridge connecting Russian-annexed Crimea to Russia caused the highway section to collapse into the sea on November 17, disrupting both road traffic and shipping between the Black Sea and Sea of Azov. Russian authorities temporarily suspended bridge traffic, though rail services later resumed. The 120-meter-wide navigational channel is now completely blocked by debris.

Ukrainian military experts say the strike systematically disrupts Russian logistics, potentially reducing attacks from Crimea on southern Ukraine. The bridge served as a supply route for weapons including ballistic missiles, guided missiles, and kamikaze drones launched from Crimean sites toward Ukrainian regions. Experts estimate rebuilding could take one and a half to three years, with ongoing Ukrainian strikes likely to impede repairs.

cards.headline: Mary Peltola defeats Dan Sullivan in Alaska Senate race, becoming first Alaska Native elected to U.S. Senate
cards.teaser: Former Democratic Representative Mary Peltola defeated two-term Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska's Senate race, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from Alas
cards.body:
Former Democratic Representative Mary Peltola defeated two-term Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska's Senate race, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from Alas

Senate, the Associated Press projects. The victory extends a series of Democratic wins in states President Donald Trump carried in 2024, including Texas, Ohio, Iowa, and South Carolina.

cards.headline: ICJ set to rule on Myanmar genocide as US threatens sanctions on judges
cards.teaser: The court will decide Thursday whether Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, amid warnings from Washington against judges including Nobel laureate Navi Pillay.
cards.body:
The International Court of Justice will rule Thursday on whether Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya during military assaults in Rakhine state in 2016 and 2017. The court has never found a state responsible for genocide, with proving intent a central challenge in past cases.

US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz warned the court's judges, including ad hoc judge Navi Pillay, that Washington will not allow what he called a lowered legal threshold for genocide that could later be applied against US or allied forces. The US and Israel fear a genocide finding could set precedent for other cases, including allegations against Israel in Gaza.

cards.headline: Prince Harry says he would rejoin military, warns of Russian threat to Europe
cards.teaser: The Duke of Sussex spoke after a surprise visit to Ukraine, calling for increased support and unity.
cards.body:
Prince Harry said he would rejoin the military if asked and warned of a growing threat from Russia following a surprise visit to Ukraine over the weekend. Speaking to the Telegraph, the Duke of Sussex said the threat to Europe had existed for 15 years and called for doubling support for Ukraine, adding that Europe risks being divided and could turn on itself without unity.

Harry visited Lviv on Saturday and Sunday, where he met injured service members and told Ukrainian hosts they would win the war against Russia, which has lasted more than four years. He suggested American public support for Ukraine remains high despite differing views within the previous administration, and expressed hope for increased U.S. support following recent mid-term elections.

cards.headline: EU halts talks on long-term UK relationship until Burnham clarifies Brexit direction
cards.teaser: European diplomats say piecemeal reset approach has reached its limits and demand clarity before further negotiations.
cards.body:
European diplomats say piecemeal reset approach has reached its limits and demand clarity before further negotiations.

European Union diplomats said they will suspend discussions with Prime Minister Andy Burnham on the UK's long-term relationship with the bloc until the British government decides whether to pursue reversing Brexit. European capitals said they have reached the end of piecemeal reset summits and want Burnham to focus on domestic decisions before proceeding, though a joint statement after a summit Friday will signal further discussions on energy markets, migration, and defense.

cards.headline: Prince William and Princess Catherine meet Indian Prime Minister Modi as they conclude three-day tour
cards.teaser: The royal couple discussed UK-India bilateral ties with Narendra Modi in New Delhi on the final day of their visit.
cards.body:
Prince William and Princess Catherine met with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Wednesday as they concluded their three-day visit to India, their first international tour since 2022. During the meeting at Modi's residence, the royals and the prime minister discussed the strength of UK-India bilateral relations and opportunities to strengthen the partnership, according to a Kensington Palace spokesperson.

Modi thanked Prince William for bringing his Earthshot Prize environmental award ceremony to India. The couple awarded £1 million in prizes to winners in Mumbai earlier in the tour. Catherine also visited a maternity hospital, where she comforted a mother who lost one premature twin. The couple last visited India in 2016.

hero.headline: Central Florida faces flooding threat through Friday as heavy rain continues across multiple counties
hero.teaser: Central Florida is under a flood watch through Friday as several more days of heavy rain threaten multiple counties already saturated by recent storms. The watch covers Volusia, Se
hero.body:
Central Florida is under a flood watch through Friday as several more days of heavy rain threaten multiple counties already saturated by recent storms. The watch covers Volusia, Seminole, Orange, Osceola, Flagler, Okeechobee, Brevard, Indian River, St. Lucie, and Martin counties, with the heaviest additional rainfall forecast along coastal areas.

Over the past 24 hours, several communities recorded significant rainfall totals. Port Orange measured 3.32 inches, while Daytona Beach received 2.21 inches and Ponce Inlet recorded 2.18 inches. Cocoa and Viera saw 1.99 inches and 1.95 inches respectively. Wednesday's forecast called for periods of showers and thunderstorms, with heavier rain possible across portions of Volusia, Seminole, Orange, Osceola, and Brevard counties. Repeated rounds of rain increase the risk of localized flooding, particularly in areas that have already received substantial precipitation.

The weather system is expected to bring sustained winds between 15 and 25 miles per hour, with gusts reaching 30 miles per hour. Wednesday through Friday are being designated as severe weather warning days for coastal communities. Drier conditions are forecast to return Saturday, with rain chances dropping to 30 percent, followed by mostly sunny weather Sunday.

The flooding threat comes two weeks after Brevard County experienced more than 20 inches of rain in some areas. Palm Bay is still dealing with cleanup from that earlier storm system.

hero.headline: Nvidia interim CEO tells employees to move forward at first all-hands meeting since Huang resignation
hero.body:
Nvidia interim chief executive Colette Kress told employees to move forward on Wednesday during the company's first all-hands meeting since founder Jensen Huang resigned, according to an attendee who spoke to CNBC. Kress was joined by newly appointed board chair Harvey Jones and hyperscale and high-performance computing head Ian Buck, along with several other senior executives. The meeting lasted about an hour and was held in person and streamed on Microsoft Teams.

Kress opened with the message about moving forward and announced that the yearly review process would be moved up from March to December, when employees typically receive pay raises and stock grants. Jones discussed the search for the next chief executive. Nvidia shares are down 37 percent from their 52-week high.

Employees have spoken up on social media in recent days to call for the return of Huang as chief executive, and one senior employee reportedly sent a letter to the board warning Nvidia would lose irreplaceable talent if it does not consider reinstating Huang. One attendee said the general sentiment in the room was that employees want Huang to come back. Another person familiar with the matter disagreed, saying that employees welcomed the remarks from leadership and the visibility into company leadership.

Jones said during the earnings call on Tuesday that the Nvidia board unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and does not intend to reinstate him as chief executive. Some executives disagreed with the statement, with one employee questioning why Jones would make such a definitive statement while the investigation is still playing out. The meeting came one day after Huang said he was ready to return as chief executive should the board want him. Multiple employees said Huang's letter fired employees up. The executives did not answer questions during Wednesday's all-hands meeting.

cards.headline: UK household energy bills forecast to rise 26% in January as inflation climbs
cards.teaser: Gas and electricity bills in the United Kingdom are forecast to jump by £443 per year starting in January as energy costs continue to push up the country's inflation rate. The annu
cards.body:
Gas and electricity bills in the United Kingdom are forecast to jump by £443 per year starting in January as energy costs continue to push up the country's inflation rate. The annu

The annual price cap on gas and electricity is predicted to rise by 26% in the new year, according to researchers at consultancy Cornwall Insight. Energy regulator Ofgem will announce the new cap on November 25.

cards.headline: Chase, Wells Fargo, Bank of America customers report service outages
cards.teaser: Thousands of customers at major U.S. banks reported trouble accessing services Monday afternoon, with Chase Bank citing a software bug in its hardware systems as a likely cause. Ch
cards.body:
Thousands of customers at major U.S. banks reported trouble accessing services Monday afternoon, with Chase Bank citing a software bug in its hardware systems as a likely cause. Ch

Chase, the largest banking institution in the country, said the issue was temporary and not systemic or cyber-related. The outages also affected Wells Fargo and Bank of America, though Chase said the bug in its systems may have impacted other banks as well.

cards.headline: Nvidia delays routine SEC filing amid internal investigation into ousted CEO
cards.teaser: The chipmaker postponed its quarterly 10-Q report, with an analyst saying the delay relates to disclosures about its probe of former CEO Jensen Huang.
cards.body:
Nvidia will not immediately file its quarterly 10-Q report with the Securities and Exchange Commission, interim CEO Colette Kress said Tuesday without explanation. UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri later revealed the company told him the delay relates to whether additional information about its ongoing investigation into former CEO Jensen Huang must be disclosed. The announcement came as The Wall Street Journal reported the SEC is investigating whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors.

Nvidia typically files the detailed quarterly report on the same day it announces earnings. The company is conducting an internal investigation into Huang after he admitted to an affair with an executive whose company is suspected of selling restricted AI chips to China. Nvidia faces multiple federal probes related to those allegations.

cards.headline: Anduril CEO says Nvidia board ousting Jensen Huang benefits China, as 200,000 sign petition for reinstatement
cards.teaser: Palmer Luckey argues removing Huang after 33 years weakens U.S. chip leadership while China seeks to challenge Nvidia's dominance with domestic chipmakers.
cards.body:
Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey said Nvidia's board is benefiting China by removing co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, who stepped down last week after 33 years amid controversy including an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy investigated for smuggling Nvidia chips. Speaking at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Luckey said China wants Huang removed to weaken American chip leadership and help its domestic semiconductor industry challenge Nvidia's dominance.

More than 200,000 people, including Elon Musk and several tech CEOs, have signed a petition calling for Huang's reinstatement. Nvidia executives said Tuesday the company does not plan to reappoint Huang, though he offered to return. Interim CEO Colette Kress announced Nvidia will stop selling H200 chips in China entirely.

cards.headline: Palmer Luckey warns AI-powered cyberattacks outpacing defenses
cards.teaser: The Anduril co-founder said adversaries including North Korea are exploiting the gap between new attack capabilities and outdated systems.
cards.body:
Palmer Luckey said AI-powered cyberattacks are moving faster than outdated technology systems can defend against them, speaking Wednesday at The New York Times DealBook Summit. The Oculus founder and Anduril Industries co-founder said adversaries including North Korea are exploiting the mismatch between new attack capabilities and defense capabilities, carrying out attacks for strategic and financial reasons.

Luckey said AI could eventually give defenders the upper hand, but only if they move more quickly to adopt new technology. He addressed the recent spate of tech outages, which government officials largely attributed to companies rushing to patch systems against new vulnerabilities AI has discovered.

cards.headline: Microsoft CEO predicts AI agents will reshape internet business models
cards.teaser: Satya Nadella says ad-driven companies will face a reshuffling as AI shopping agents change web economics.
cards.body:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said Wednesday that AI agents will reshape internet economics and disrupt advertising-driven business models built for human web traffic. Speaking at The New York Times Dealbook Summit, Nadella said companies may need to shift from advertising revenue to transaction-based models, warning that businesses refusing AI agents risk losing ground to competitors.

Nadella cited Amazon's decision to block AI agents from browsing its retail site and making purchases as an example. He suggested that if Amazon continues blocking agents, rivals like Shopify could gain an advantage by allowing them access. Nadella compared the shift to the earlier transition from web portals to search engines.

cards.headline: Microsoft releases Windows Server 2028 Public Preview with security-by-default configuration
cards.teaser: The server operating system ships with Defense Department-aligned hardening standards and post-quantum cryptography enabled from installation.
cards.body:
Microsoft released a public preview of Windows Server 2028 with security configurations aligned to Defense Information Systems Agency hardening standards enabled by default. The new approach reverses the traditional model in which administrators applied security settings after installation, eliminating the exposure window for newly deployed servers.

The hardened-by-default state applies only to Server Core installations and includes Kerberos authentication over NTLM, restricted TLS cipher suites, and hybrid post-quantum key exchange based on ML-KEM. Administrators retain control over which security protocols remain active, but the operating system now ships in a pre-hardened configuration rather than requiring manual implementation of recommended baselines.

cards.headline: Nvidia now generates $8,300 in profit every second despite Jensen Huang's resignation
cards.teaser: The chipmaker produces $65 billion in quarterly profit from AI demand, dwarfing earlier crypto and GPU shortage peaks.
cards.body:
Nvidia generates approximately $8,300 in profit every second, totaling $65 billion per quarter as artificial intelligence demand drives unprecedented growth. The company's profitability far exceeds earlier peaks during the cryptocurrency boom and graphics processing unit shortage, when quarterly profits reached $3 billion. Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive in early November following scandals, causing Nvidia's market value to drop from $5 trillion to $3.6 trillion.

Interim chief executive Colette Kress said the company projects $130 billion in revenue next quarter and plans to return all excess cash to shareholders. A $1,000 investment in Nvidia a decade ago would now be worth over $67,000. Kress said Nvidia expects continued growth, with gross margins targeted at 73 percent next year.

hero.headline: Georgia attorney general urges SEC action against LSU over disputed player eligibility
hero.body:
Georgia Attorney General Chris Carr has asked the Southeastern Conference to take action against Louisiana State University over the school's decision to roster basketball player RJ Luis Jr., escalating a dispute over the former St. John's guard who signed contracts with NBA teams. Carr's letter accuses LSU of showing contempt for conference rules.

Luis, an All-American transfer, is at the center of a legal and administrative fight over his NCAA eligibility after signing professional contracts. LSU added Luis to its basketball roster despite the SEC's objections and an ongoing court battle over whether his prior NBA agreements disqualify him from collegiate competition. The conference has expressed frustration with LSU's actions.

The dispute has reached a point where some SEC members are considering boycotting games against LSU if head coach Will Wade plays Luis on the court, according to reports. The potential boycotts would represent an extraordinary escalation in the standoff between the conference and one of its member institutions.

The case tests NCAA rules governing player compensation and professional contracts at a time when college athletics is navigating rapidly changing policies around athlete earnings. LSU maintains it will keep Luis on its roster, while the SEC and state officials from other member states argue the university is violating eligibility standards that apply across the conference.

cards.headline: England defender Jess Carter signs with Bay FC through 2028
cards.teaser: The international joins the NWSL club after leaving reigning regular-season champion Gotham FC as a free agent.
cards.body:
England international defender Jess Carter has signed with Bay FC through 2028, with an option for an additional year, after leaving Gotham FC as a free agent. The 29-year-old, who has 56 caps for England, played in all 30 matches for Gotham in 2026 as the club won the NWSL Shield as regular-season champions.

Carter joined Gotham in July 2024 after six years with Chelsea, where she won five Women's Super League titles. She helped Gotham win the 2025 NWSL Championship and was part of England's squad that won the 2022 European Championship. The 2027 NWSL season begins in February.

cards.headline: Emma Hayes to advise US Soccer's search for next USMNT head coach
cards.teaser: The USWNT coach confirms her role in selecting Mauricio Pochettino's replacement following his departure to Manchester United.
cards.body:
US women's national team head coach Emma Hayes confirmed she will assist in the search for Mauricio Pochettino's replacement as men's national team coach following his departure to Manchester United. Hayes said US Soccer CEO JT Batson asked her to participate as a technical voice alongside Batson, chief operating officer Dan Helfrich, and vice president of sporting Oguchi Onyewu.

Hayes, who took over the USWNT in 2024 and led the team to Olympic gold, said her role is to support the process through a technical lens based on her 25 years of coaching experience. She praised Pochettino's work and emphasized the importance of a thorough search process to build on the foundation he established.

cards.headline: Bottas retained by Cadillac for 2027 Formula 1 season despite pointless debut
cards.teaser: The Finnish driver will return despite Cadillac's scoreless maiden campaign.
cards.body:
Valtteri Bottas has been retained by Cadillac for the 2027 Formula 1 season despite the American team's winless debut year. The 37-year-old Finn's future had been uncertain as Cadillac has failed to score a point in either championship this season.

Bottas, a two-time championship runner-up, said the team is building foundations and learning. The announcement follows Cadillac's recent confirmation that Sergio Perez will remain with the team through 2029.

cards.headline: Defending champion Luke Littler eliminated from Grand Slam of Darts in upset
cards.teaser: The 19-year-old world champion fell 10-8 to 16th seed Jermaine Wattimena in the second round in Wolverhampton.
cards.body:
Defending champion Luke Littler was eliminated from the Grand Slam of Darts after losing 10-8 to 16th seed Jermaine Wattimena in the second round in Wolverhampton. The 38-year-old Dutchman dominated early, winning six consecutive legs to take a 7-2 lead, and finished with an average of 101.70 and 10 maximum 180s scores.

Littler mounted a late comeback after Wattimena faltered one leg from victory, but the 19-year-old world champion could not complete the rally. Wattimena closed out the match by hitting double-20 to finish with 77 points remaining, advancing to the quarterfinals where he will face compatriot Kevin Doets.

cards.headline: Mudryk blames Ukraine football association for failed drug test
cards.teaser: Tottenham winger says banned substance entered his system during national team duty.
cards.body:
On-loan Tottenham winger Mykhailo Mudryk said he blames Ukraine's football association for the failed drug test that led to his ban, in his first detailed public comments since returning to the sport. The 25-year-old tested positive for meldonium in November 2024 and was suspended until July 2026 after accepting he had breached anti-doping rules.

Mudryk told a Ukrainian YouTube channel that meldonium is only available in Eastern Europe and could only have entered his body while he was with the national team in Ukraine. He also criticized Ukrainian Association of Football president Andriy Shevchenko for offering little support and blamed the association for leaks that delayed his return to football.

cards.headline: English FA explored legal challenge to Infantino fourth term, decided against it
cards.teaser: The Football Association considered challenging Gianni Infantino's eligibility to run for a fourth FIFA presidency but concluded a challenge would likely fail.
cards.body:
The English Football Association considered challenging Gianni Infantino's eligibility to run for a fourth term as FIFA president but concluded such a challenge would likely fail, BBC Sport reported. Infantino oversaw the introduction of a three-term limit when he replaced Sepp Blatter, but FIFA's council ruled in 2022 that his initial period from 2016 to 2019 should not count as a full term because it completed his predecessor's interrupted tenure.

FA chair Debbie Hewitt told human rights group Fair Square that the association explored the possibility but does not believe a challenge would succeed, as the process followed FIFA's governance rules. The FA said it remains opposed to Infantino's reelection and supports rival candidate Philippe Diallo, president of the French Football Federation, in the March election.

hero.headline: Cascio siblings sue Michael Jackson estate attorney for malpractice over 2019 abuse settlement
hero.body:
Five siblings who allege Michael Jackson sexually abused them as children have sued entertainment attorney Bryan Freedman for legal malpractice, claiming he deceived them into signing a 2019 agreement that silenced their abuse allegations while shielding Jackson's estate from liability. The lawsuit was filed Wednesday in Los Angeles County Superior Court.

Frank Cascio and his siblings Dominic, Marie-Nicole, Edward, and Aldo allege Freedman exploited their vulnerability to secure the agreement after Jackson's estate sought to contain fallout from the documentary Leaving Neverland. The siblings claim Freedman, who was already representing two family members in unrelated matters, assured them he was acting in their best interests while discouraging them from hiring independent counsel. They say he failed to disclose provisions barring them from publicly discussing the alleged abuse and releasing the estate from liability related to it.

Under the agreement, the estate was to pay each sibling $690,000 annually for five years, with disputes subject to mandatory arbitration. The lawsuit alleges Freedman never explained the payment was inadequate compared to amounts Jackson and the estate paid other alleged victims, nor did he disclose a penalty provision requiring the entire family to return all payments if one member disclosed Jackson's alleged crimes. The siblings also claim Freedman later returned in 2024 calling the original agreement "toilet paper" and said the estate wanted to pay them more.

The siblings recognized a conflict of interest, hired new representation, and informed the estate they would challenge the agreement. They filed a child sex trafficking lawsuit in February that was ordered into arbitration in August. The new complaint against Freedman, filed by attorney Howard King, includes claims for breach of fiduciary duty, fraud, and negligent misrepresentation. A lawyer for Jackson's estate has previously called the siblings' allegations a "desperate money grab" and noted the family defended Jackson for more than 25 years.

cards.headline: Museum of Fine Arts Boston to open first exhibit devoted to a musician with Taylor Swift collection
cards.teaser: The exhibit features over 50 outfits and instruments spanning Swift's career and 12 albums, opening April 10.
cards.body:
The Museum of Fine Arts, Boston announced Wednesday it will showcase "Taylor Swift: The Eras Collection," the museum's first exhibition devoted to a musician. The exhibit, running from April 10 through August, will feature more than 50 outfits, instruments, and sketches from Swift's performances, music videos, and tours.

The collection includes Swift's custom red Alberta Ferretti gown from folklore and evermore, a 2022 bedazzled bodysuit from Zuhair Murad, and the tinsel fringe jacket from the Eras Tour "Karma" finale. Instruments on display include a Deering banjo from the 2010 Speak Now World Tour and a Gibson acoustic guitar from the 2017 Reputation Stadium Tour. Tickets are $40 and go on sale December 13.

cards.headline: Michelle Monaghan replaces Parker Posey in Blumhouse horror film 'Sleepover'
cards.teaser: Monaghan will star opposite Justin Theroux in the film, directed by Jacob Chase and scheduled for October 2027 release.
cards.body:
Michelle Monaghan will star opposite Justin Theroux in "Sleepover," a horror film from Blumhouse Atomic and Universal Pictures set for theatrical release in October 2027. Monaghan was cast after Parker Posey dropped out of the project, with Posey telling NBC's "Today" that "something came up."

Jacob Chase, who directed "Insidious: Out of the Further," is directing from a script he co-wrote with Bryce McGuire, based on McGuire's original short story. Plot details remain undisclosed. Jason Blum serves as producer on the project, which reunites Chase and Blumhouse Atomic after their previous collaboration on the sixth "Insidious" installment.

cards.headline: Beach Boys co-founder Al Jardine writes open letter supporting Mike Love amid health decline
cards.teaser: Jardine publicly expressed support for his longtime bandmate, who has not been seen since October after canceled tour dates.
cards.body:
Beach Boys co-founder Al Jardine published an open letter to bandmate Mike Love, who has been dealing with serious health issues. Jardine quoted lyrics from the 1968 song "Friends" and wrote he was "praying for your recovery." Love has not been seen in public since an October concert in Nashville, and the Beach Boys' remaining 2026 dates have been canceled.

Jardine and Love are the last surviving members of the original Beach Boys lineup but have had a contentious relationship marked by legal disputes and acrimony following a 2012 reunion tour. Love was unable to stand or sing at October performances in Nashville and Cincinnati before the tour was halted.

cards.headline: Perez Hilton making progress in recovery, family says
cards.teaser: The celebrity blogger has completed a partial hospitalization program and moved to outpatient care months after an August hospitalization.
cards.body:
Perez Hilton has completed a partial hospitalization program and moved to outpatient care, his family said Wednesday, months after the celebrity blogger was hospitalized following acts of self-harm during an August TikTok livestream. Hilton finished the inpatient program in October and has moved back in with family while continuing intensive outpatient mental health treatment.

Hilton has had several weekend visits with his mother and children in recent weeks. His family said he is making encouraging progress and moving gradually toward a full return to his life. Hilton was hospitalized August 4 after Miami-Dade fire rescue treated him for multiple lacerations and an overdose.

cards.headline: John Mayer, Brad Paisley join Michael J. Fox for 'Johnny B. Goode' at Parkinson's fundraiser
cards.teaser: The musicians performed the Chuck Berry song Fox famously played in Back to the Future at a New York gala.
cards.body:
John Mayer and Brad Paisley joined Michael J. Fox onstage Saturday night for a performance of Chuck Berry's "Johnny B. Goode" at Fox's Parkinson's research fundraiser in New York. The song featured prominently in the climax of Back to the Future. The performance took place at the Waldorf Astoria as part of Fox's A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to Cure Parkinson's gala.

Mayer sang lead vocals while Fox played guitar alongside Paisley and other musicians. After the performance, Fox thanked the musicians in an emotional speech. Mayer has said the Back to the Future scene inspired him to play guitar, and he previously performed the song with Fox in 2013.

cards.headline: Snoh Aalegra releases Legendary Love, her first album in five years
cards.teaser: The R&B singer worked with Nile Rodgers, Babyface, and others on the 13-track project inspired by unrequited love.
cards.body:
R&B singer Snoh Aalegra released Legendary Love, her first album in five years, following an extended period focused on processing unrequited love. The Iranian-born, Swedish-raised artist worked on the 13-track album in Los Angeles with collaborators including Joel Compass, Mustafa, Daniel Caesar, Raphael Saadiq, Babyface, and Nile Rodgers.

The album draws heavily on 1980s influences, particularly the sounds associated with Prince and Janet Jackson. Aalegra secured approval for a Stevie Wonder sample and received input from Jimmy Jam on the track "Nothing Compares." She said the project was intended to be heard as a complete body of work.

hero.headline: Laurel Lee seeks top GOP spot on House Judiciary as Democrats signal Trump investigations
hero.body:
Representative Laurel Lee announced Wednesday her bid to lead Republicans on the House Judiciary Committee, a position that would place her at the center of potential Democratic efforts to impeach President Donald Trump. The Florida Republican told colleagues in a letter that she understands the constitutional grounds for impeachment and can distinguish between policy disagreements and impeachable offenses.

Lee cited her background as a judge, federal prosecutor, and former Florida secretary of state as qualifications for the role. She said she is prepared to make distinctions about impeachment in committee hearings and explain them to the public. She also told colleagues she is equipped to respond to investigations that committee Democrats, led by incoming Chair Jamie Raskin of Maryland, have already indicated they plan to pursue.

If recommended by the House GOP Steering Committee, Lee would be among the few Republican women in leadership roles in the House. She was elected to Congress in 2022.

Lee is expected to compete against Representatives Lance Gooden of Texas and Scott Fitzgerald of Wisconsin for the position.

cards.headline: Mary Peltola defeats Dan Sullivan in Alaska Senate race, becoming first Alaska Native elected to U.S. Senate
cards.teaser: Former Democratic Representative Mary Peltola defeated two-term Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska's Senate race, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from Alas
cards.body:
Former Democratic Representative Mary Peltola defeated two-term Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska's Senate race, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from Alas

Senate, the Associated Press projects. The victory extends a series of Democratic wins in states President Donald Trump carried in 2024, including Texas, Ohio, Iowa, and South Carolina.
